clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man presented with bilateral flank pain, urinary symptoms (frequency, foamy urine), and dyspnea on exertion, with a history of anterior uveitis diagnosed one week prior. Initial workup revealed acute kidney injury (creatinine 2.3 mg/dL, eGFR 30.9 mL/min). Renal ultrasound showed elevated parenchymal echogenicity. Renal biopsy confirmed diffuse tubulointerstitial nephritis with lymphocytic and eosinophilic infiltrates, negative immunofluorescence, and no electron-dense deposits. Ophthalmologic examination confirmed bilateral anterior uveitis with anterior chamber inflammatory cells. The diagnosis of TINU syndrome was established based on the characteristic association of tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis, and the patient was treated with topical corticosteroids with good control of ocular inflammation.
